title: All of Us Research Program: diversity-oriented genomics and phenotype denominator rail
summary: Infrastructure record for All of Us as a large-scale, diversity-oriented U.S. biomedical data rail with genomic, EHR, survey, and workbench access surfaces.

status_history.note: Added as diversity/denominator correction rail in genomics scope pass.

place.scope: United States longitudinal research cohort and data resource; not a global-genomics completion claim

claims.claim: The All of Us genomics data release describes a longitudinal cohort aiming to enrol at least one million diverse U.S. participants; it reports 245,388 clinical-grade genome sequences, 77% of participants from historically under-represented biomedical communities, 46% from under-represented racial and ethnic minorities, and more than one billion genetic variants.
what_would_change_status: Second-pass source review or newer primary evidence materially changes the claim scope.

claims.claim: The same article describes public summary-level data, individual-level Researcher Workbench access, more than 413,000 participants in the fifth data release, and rich participant data combining surveys, physical measurements, EHRs, wearables, and genomic data.
what_would_change_status: Second-pass source review or newer primary evidence materially changes the claim scope.

claims.claim: All of Us is encoded as a correction rail, not a solution: the article emphasizes open science, equitable access, data-passport governance, participant protection, and regular future releases, which makes it a denominator-expansion infrastructure rather than proof that genomic evidence is now fully representative.
what_would_change_status: Second-pass source review or newer primary evidence materially changes the claim scope.

type_payload.signal_capture_model: large-scale consented longitudinal participant data with genomics, EHR, surveys, public summary browser, and controlled researcher workbench access
limitations: United States scope, not global representativeness.
Access/governance/participant trust are part of the evidence object.
Data availability does not guarantee equitable clinical implementation.

handling_notes: Participant privacy, consent, return-of-results, and access governance are part of the record.
Do not treat U.S. diversity as global representativeness.

unknowns: No workbench terms-of-use or data-access policy second-pass review.
No updated 2026 release status is encoded beyond the 2024 article.
next_actions: Add current official All of Us data-release status source if needed.
Pair with H3Africa and global south resources in a denominator-diversity infrastructure map.

scope_qualifiers.ancestry_or_population_scope: U.S. diversity-oriented cohort, not global representativeness
scope_qualifiers.portability_caution: data resource does not guarantee equitable implementation
